collection_summary: This instance is a curator-bounded ground truth listing 12 major religious traditions commonly covered in world-religions textbook surveys, with each tradition's canonical foundational text or corpus, the scriptural language(s) of original composition, and the tradition family (Abrahamic / Dharmic / East Asian / Iranian). The 12-row universe is a balanced textbook-canon slate (4 Abrahamic + 4 Dharmic + 3 East Asian + 1 Iranian) honestly characterized as candidate_rebuild rather than source-defined — no single Wikipedia master article enumerates this exact 12-row slate, and the Wikipedia 'World religions' article explicitly says 'world religion' is a socially-constructed category. The schema is designed for qualitative benchmark evaluation: Religion is the PK lookup target; Foundational Text is text exact-match (single canonical title or corpus name per religion); Scriptural Language(s) is text exact-match with semicolon-delimited values for multi-language corpora; Tradition Family is exact-match from a closed 4-value vocabulary.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (World_religions): universe-context (defines the 'world religions' socially-constructed category typically referring to the Big Five Christianity / Islam / Hinduism / Buddhism / Judaism with extensions to Bahá'í Faith / Sikhism / Zoroastrianism per the article's classification section — provides the textbook-canon slate framing rationale).
- source_urls[1] (Major_religious_groups): tradition-family taxonomy support (provides the Abrahamic / Dharmic / East Asian / Iranian classification taxonomy used for the Tradition Family column).
- source_urls[2] (List_of_religious_texts): text-candidate master (lists per-religion canonical texts under tradition-family section headings — provides the source-listed candidate corpora for the Foundational Text column).
- source_urls[3] (Kitáb-i-Aqdas): per-text source for Bahá'í Faith row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Kitáb-i-Aqdas' and Scriptural Language = 'Arabic' verbatim from the article's lead).
- source_urls[4] (Tripitaka): per-text source for Buddhism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Tripitaka' and Scriptural Language(s) = 'Pali; Sanskrit; Buddhist Chinese; Tibetan' from the article's three-canon scope; the Tripitaka article documents that surviving Tripitaka literature is in Pali with some in Sanskrit, that the Chinese Buddhist Canon was translated into 'Buddhist Chinese, a form of traditional literary Chinese', and that the Tibetan Buddhist Canon comprises Kangyur/Tengyur material in Tibetan — the cell uses the article's own wording 'Buddhist Chinese' and 'Tibetan' rather than the more-generic 'Classical Chinese' / 'Classical Tibetan').
- source_urls[5] (Bible): per-text source for Christianity row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Bible' and Scriptural Language(s) = 'Biblical Hebrew; Biblical Aramaic; Koine Greek' per the Bible article's lead and New Testament section; the Bible article documents Hebrew + Aramaic + Greek as the three original-composition languages of the canonical biblical corpus).
- source_urls[6] (Four_Books_and_Five_Classics): per-text source for Confucianism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Four Books and Five Classics' and Scriptural Language = 'Classical Chinese' per the article's compilation language).
- source_urls[7] (Vedas): per-text source for Hinduism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Vedas' as the broadest Śruti corpus and Scriptural Language = 'Vedic Sanskrit' verbatim from the article's lead).
- source_urls[8] (Quran): per-text source for Islam row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Quran' and Scriptural Language = 'Classical Arabic' verbatim from the article's lead).
- source_urls[9] (Jain_Agamas): per-text source for Jainism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Agamas' and Scriptural Language = 'Ardhamagadhi Prakrit' verbatim from the article's lead).
- source_urls[10] (Tanakh): per-text source for Judaism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Tanakh' and Scriptural Language(s) = 'Biblical Hebrew; Biblical Aramaic' per the article's language section).
- source_urls[11] (Kojiki): per-text source for Shinto row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Kojiki' as the older of the two Shinto chronicles, and Scriptural Language(s) = 'Classical Chinese; Old Japanese' per the article's language section noting the prose is mostly Classical Chinese with songs in Old Japanese via man'yōgana).
- source_urls[12] (Guru_Granth_Sahib): per-text source for Sikhism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Guru Granth Sahib' and Scriptural Language(s) = 'Sant Bhasha; multiple Indo-Aryan languages; Persian; Arabic' as a compact-semantic compression of the article's larger language inventory including Punjabi, Lahnda, regional Prakrits, Apabhramsa, Sanskrit, Hindi-Braj, Bhojpuri, Sindhi, Marathi, Marwari, Bengali, Persian, Arabic — Gurmukhi is the SCRIPT not a language and is therefore NOT in the Scriptural Language(s) cell).
- source_urls[13] (Tao_Te_Ching): per-text source for Taoism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Tao Te Ching' as the most-famous individual Taoist text per textbook tradition, and Scriptural Language = 'Classical Chinese' verbatim from the article's lead — Tao Te Ching is selected over the broader Daozang corpus per the audit-noted exception rule for individual-text-over-broad-corpus where the individual text is significantly more LLM-canonical).
- source_urls[14] (Avesta): per-text source for Zoroastrianism row (supplies Foundational Text = 'Avesta' and Scriptural Language = 'Avestan' verbatim from the article's lead).

Multi-source Tier B instance (source_count = 15 = 3 master + 12 per-text). The three master Wikipedia articles supply universe-context (World_religions), tradition-family taxonomy (Major_religious_groups), and text-candidate enumeration (List_of_religious_texts). The 12 per-text Wikipedia articles ground the answer-key Foundational Text and Scriptural Language(s) cells — each text's dedicated article supplies the canonical title and the language(s) of original composition. Cell-level audit can spot-check the Religion + Tradition Family cells against source_urls[0]/[1]; the Foundational Text + Scriptural Language(s) cells can be spot-checked against the per-text source listed in this Roles block.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass (after extensive pre-staging design review by audit agent — see post-audit cycle-0 notes below). Universe (12 textbook-canon major religious traditions) is honestly characterized as curator-bounded candidate_rebuild rather than source-defined 'major world religions'; per-row attribute cells are verbatim/lightly-normalized from per-text Wikipedia articles (with one semicolon-delimited multi-language cell and one compact-semantic-compression cell for Sikhism). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical Big Five foundational texts; mid-difficulty cells include the textbook-canonical extensions; harder calibration cells include the less-LLM-knowable corpora and the language-cell normalizations. Row count (12) clears the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected after picker recommendation for 'chip qualitative to gap-1' option; pre-staging audit review surfaced 4 design-level issues that were addressed before cycle-0 staging.
- Category: qualitative (gap 2 before this staging — `qualitative` at 3 of 5 with major_music_genres_landmark_albums, major_western_philosophers_primary_works, us_states_warm_year_round_climate; this instance brings qualitative to 4/5 — gap 2 → 1).
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, multi-source; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 15 (3 master + 12 per-text).
- Expected shape: 12 rows × 4 columns; PK = Religion.
- Domain: Religion/Texts — NEW Texts subdomain extending the Religion family from 2 to 3 instances (existing: Religion/Holy Sites via world_religions_top5_holy_sites; Religion/Mythology via twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman).
- Entity class: abstract-categories/religions — existing fine-class (already represented by world_religions_top5_holy_sites which uses religions as the per-row partition); this is the 2nd religions-keyed instance.
- Risks/adaptation: (a) curator-bounded universe — the 12-row textbook-canon slate is principled (Big Five + Bahá'í/Sikhism/Zoroastrianism per Wikipedia 'World religions' classification section + Taoism/Confucianism/Shinto + Jainism for textbook-canon East Asian and Dharmic completeness) but not source-defined; honestly signaled via claim_type = candidate_rebuild. (b) Foundational Text precedence rule: 'Prefer the broadest named canonical corpus listed under the religion in List of religious texts; for traditions where a single individual text is more LLM-canonical than the broader corpus, use the individual text and document the exception in normalization_decisions' — 3 such per-row exceptions documented (Bahá'í Kitáb-i-Aqdas, Taoism Tao Te Ching, Shinto Kojiki). (c) Scriptural Language(s) column uses semicolon-delimited multi-language cells for corpora composed in multiple languages; one row (Sikhism Guru Granth Sahib) uses compact-semantic compression of the per-text article's larger language inventory. (d) Tradition Family 4-value taxonomy: Bahá'í documented as Abrahamic-by-origin (post-Islamic, founded 1844-1863); Sikhism documented as Dharmic per Indian-origin and shared dharma concepts; Confucianism included per world-religions textbook convention despite philosophy-vs-religion debate.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets religious traditions, sacred texts, or qualitative religion-keyed instances.

Why 12-row textbook-canon universe rather than alternatives: pre-staging audit review compared 3 universe options. Option A (9-10 row Big-Five-plus-Bahá'í-Sikhism-Zoroastrianism, source-defined per Wikipedia 'World religions' classification) was rejected because it excludes Taoism/Confucianism/Shinto/Jainism which are textbook-canonical and would create false impression of a complete world-religions slate. Option B (12-row textbook-canon slate, the chosen design) balances source-derived 'world religions' framing with textbook-canon completeness. Option C (15-17 row expansion to include Mormonism/Tenrikyo/Rastafari/Cao Dai) was rejected because the expansion is curator-judgment without source-defined population threshold, and the new-religion additions are less LLM-canonical.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: qualitative pairs reasonably with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md. The 3-attribute SELECT per row (Foundational Text + Scriptural Language(s) + Tradition Family) over the curator-bounded entity universe is the canonical qualitative-projection primitive (matching major_western_philosophers_primary_works's 4-col SELECT pattern with similar candidate_rebuild claim_type).

Domain selection: Religion/Texts — NEW Texts subdomain extending Religion family from 2 to 3 instances. Existing Religion subdomains: Holy Sites (world_religions_top5_holy_sites scaled_enumeration) and Mythology (twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman factual_lookup). NEW Texts subdomain is the textual-canon angle complementing the existing site-keyed and mythology-keyed instances.

Entity class selection: abstract-categories/religions — already an existing fine-class (world_religions_top5_holy_sites uses religions as the per-row partition under the answer-entity-wins exception). This is the 2nd religions-keyed instance; the bucket has 3 fine-classes (music-genres, religions, languages) with religions now at 2 instances and the bucket at 4 total instances.

Claim type: candidate_rebuild — the universe is curator-bounded; no single Wikipedia master article enumerates the exact 12-row slate. The Wikipedia 'World religions' article explicitly says 'world religion' is a socially-constructed category that typically refers to the Big Five and sometimes extends to Bahá'í/Sikhism/Zoroastrianism. The staged 12-row slate is a balanced textbook-canon coverage rather than source-defined population-rank or formal-definition. claim_type matches the precedent set by major_western_philosophers_primary_works (16 philosophers, also candidate_rebuild).

Pre-staging audit review (2026-05-14): audit agent provided design-level review BEFORE cycle-0 staging and surfaced 4 issues with the initial proposal. All 4 issues addressed in this cycle-0 design BEFORE any CSV/draft/curation files were written. (a) Universe scope overclaim: initial proposal framed the 12-row universe as 'major world religions' which is too strong for a curator-bounded textbook-canon slate — audit cited Wikipedia 'Major religious groups' adherent-count tables not supporting the exact 12-row set. Resolved by reframing title to 'selected major religious traditions covered in world-religions textbook surveys' and adding 'World religions' Wikipedia article as the primary universe-context master. (b) Source plan mismatch: initial proposal used per-religion articles for Original Language grounding, but Original Language is a property of the text/corpus not the religion — audit recommended per-text articles. Resolved by revising source plan to 12 per-text articles (one per row) + 3 master articles for universe-context, taxonomy, and text-candidate enumeration. (c) Specific language-cell errors: initial proposal had wrong values for Sikhism (Gurmukhi is a SCRIPT not a language), Christianity (missing Aramaic), Judaism (missing Aramaic), and Shinto Kojiki (Classical Japanese was wrong; should be Classical Chinese + Old Japanese). All 4 cell-level errors corrected in this cycle-0 staging. (d) Foundational Text precedence rule needed: initial proposal had Buddhism Pali Canon (Theravada-specific), Confucianism Analects (one component of broader Four Books), Judaism Hebrew Bible (audit preferred Tanakh wording). All 3 revised per audit recommendation: Buddhism → Tripitaka (broader cross-tradition corpus); Confucianism → Four Books and Five Classics (broader canonical corpus); Judaism → Tanakh. Explicit text-selection precedence rule written into normalization_decisions: 'Prefer the broadest named canonical corpus listed under the religion in List of religious texts; for traditions where a single individual text is more LLM-canonical than the broader corpus, use the individual text and document the exception in normalization_decisions'.

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 1): cycle-1 audit verdict 'Not ready' — 1 BLOCKING, 2 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. (a) BLOCKING (factual) — Buddhism Scriptural Language(s) cell over-specified the cited Tripitaka source. Cycle-0 staged 'Pali; Sanskrit; Classical Chinese; Classical Tibetan' but the Tripitaka Wikipedia article uses its own wording: surviving Tripitaka literature is in Pali with some Sanskrit; Chinese Buddhist Canon is in 'Buddhist Chinese, a form of traditional literary Chinese'; Tibetan Buddhist Canon comprises Kangyur/Tengyur material in Tibetan. The cycle-0 'Classical Chinese' and 'Classical Tibetan' labels are not used by the source article. Resolved by rewriting the Buddhism cell to 'Pali; Sanskrit; Buddhist Chinese; Tibetan' matching the article's own wording. (b) HYGIENE (structural) — current-state prose cited a 'Biblical languages' Wikipedia article that is NOT in source_urls (source_urls[5] is the Bible article only). The Bible article's lead and New Testament section themselves document Hebrew + Aramaic + Greek, so the Christianity language cell is already source-grounded. Resolved by removing all 'Biblical languages article' references from temporal_note, _extraction_notes, source_coverage_notes, and normalization_decisions; the prose now cites only the Bible article (which is in source_urls). (c) HYGIENE (structural) — normalization_decisions Scriptural Language(s) paragraph said 'Single-language rows (8)' but listed 7 rows, and 'Multi-language rows (4)' but listed 5 rows. The actual CSV has 7 single-language + 5 multi-language. Resolved by correcting the counts to '7 single-language / 5 multi-language' and softening 'full canonical-language inventory' to 'canonical-language inventory per source, with documented compression allowed for corpora whose source-listed language inventory is unwieldy' (the Sikhism compact-semantic compression is the documented case). Net cycle-1 changes: 1 CSV cell rewrite (Buddhism Scriptural Language(s) row 'Classical Chinese; Classical Tibetan' → 'Buddhist Chinese; Tibetan'); 4 prose-section scrubs of 'Biblical languages' provenance reference (temporal_note, _extraction_notes, source_coverage_notes, normalization_decisions); 1 normalization_decisions count + wording fix (8/4 → 7/5 + softened 'full inventory' wording); no source_count / row count / schema / column / Tradition-Family-distribution changes (still 12 rows × 4 cols, source_count 15, Religion PK unique, alphabetical sort intact, Abrahamic 4 / Dharmic 4 / East Asian 3 / Iranian 1 intact).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 2): cycle-2 verification audit verdict 'Ready with residual hygiene' — 0 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Buddhism cell repair confirmed source-grounded; Pali/Sanskrit/Buddhist Chinese/Tibetan matches Tripitaka article wording. Residual hygiene: draft.json::temporal_note still said multi-language cells reflect 'the full canonical-language inventory per source' — the cycle-1 normalization_decisions softening of this wording was not propagated to the parallel temporal_note phrasing. Resolved by softening temporal_note multi-language description to 'reflect the canonical-language inventory per source, with documented compression allowed for corpora whose source-listed language inventory is unwieldy (the Sikhism compact-semantic compression below is the documented case)' — matching the cycle-1 wording in normalization_decisions. Net cycle-2 changes: 1 temporal_note wording softening; no CSV / source_count / row count / schema / distribution / other-prose changes (still 12 rows × 4 cols, source_count 15, Religion PK unique, alphabetical sort intact, 7 single-language + 5 multi-language distribution intact).

Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 3 re-run): cycle-3 re-run verification audit verdict 'Ready+Clean / accept-ready' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The audit agent re-read the current canonical files and confirmed the previous 'Ready with residual hygiene' finding was stale relative to the current file state: draft.json::temporal_note now uses the compression-aware wording, and the old 'full canonical-language inventory' phrase only survives in historical decision_log repair paragraphs (legitimate narrative). Buddhism cell remains 'Pali; Sanskrit; Buddhist Chinese; Tibetan' (supported by Tripitaka article's Pali/Sanskrit, Buddhist Chinese, and Tibetan canon sections); Bible provenance repair remains clean (Bible article supports Hebrew + Aramaic + Koine Greek for the corpus). Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-15. Total cycle count: 4 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-3 audit/repair, with cycle-3 having a stale-cache misfire followed by a clean re-run). Universe stable at 12 events across all cycles; the cycle history involved 1 BLOCKING (Buddhism Classical-Chinese/Tibetan label) + 2 HYGIENE (Biblical_languages article reference + 8/4 → 7/5 language count) + 1 HYGIENE (temporal_note 'full canonical-language inventory' wording) — all resolved without any row count, schema, or source-set changes. The instance chips `qualitative` from gap 2 to **gap 1** (4 of 5 staged) and adds Religion/Texts as a NEW subdomain, extending the Religion family from 2 to 3 instances. Useful reference: candidate_rebuild claim_type with curator-bounded textbook-canon universe requires extensive pre-staging design review to ensure honest characterization; the cycle-0 staging had the benefit of 4 pre-staging audit-feedback iterations resolved before any files were written, which is why the post-staging audit cycle was relatively short (3 cycles) compared to other recent multi-cycle instances (financial_crises 6 cycles, edtech 10 cycles).
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is the 12 religious traditions commonly covered in world-religions textbook surveys, balanced across the 4 tradition families: Abrahamic 4 (Bahá'í Faith, Christianity, Islam, Judaism), Dharmic 4 (Buddhism, Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism), East Asian 3 (Confucianism, Shinto, Taoism), Iranian 1 (Zoroastrianism). The universe boundary is curator-bounded textbook-canon coverage rather than source-defined population-rank: Wikipedia 'World religions' article explicitly says 'world religion' is a socially-constructed category typically referring to the Big Five (Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism) and sometimes extended to Bahá'í Faith, Sikhism, and Zoroastrianism. The staged 12-row slate extends the Wikipedia-recognized 8 (Big Five + 3 extensions) with 4 additional textbook-canonical traditions (Taoism, Confucianism, Shinto, Jainism) for balanced East Asian and Dharmic coverage. Religion name normalization: each row's Religion is taken verbatim from the corresponding Wikipedia article's canonical name (with apostrophe in 'Bahá'í Faith' preserving the diacritical marks; '(Nyasa)' and similar parenthetical alternates omitted as not present in canonical religion names). Foundational Text normalization: each row's Foundational Text is selected per the precedence rule 'Prefer the broadest named canonical corpus listed under the religion in Wikipedia's List of religious texts master article; for traditions where a single individual text is more LLM-canonical than the broader corpus, use the individual text and document the exception below'. Broadest-corpus selections (9 of 12 rows): Bible (Christianity, full canon Hebrew + Greek), Tanakh (Judaism, Hebrew Bible), Tripitaka (Buddhism, cross-tradition canon covering Theravada Pali Canon + East Asian Mahayana + Tibetan canons), Vedas (Hinduism, oldest Śruti corpus), Quran (Islam, single canonical book), Guru Granth Sahib (Sikhism, single canonical text compiled 1604), Agamas (Jainism, foundational corpus), Avesta (Zoroastrianism, Avestan-language canonical corpus), Four Books and Five Classics (Confucianism, broadest canonical Confucian corpus). Individual-text exceptions (3 of 12 rows): Bahá'í Faith Kitáb-i-Aqdas (selected over Bahá'u'lláh's full writings corpus because Kitáb-i-Aqdas is the single most-authoritative legal-doctrinal book and is the most-LLM-canonical Bahá'í text); Taoism Tao Te Ching (selected over the broader Daozang corpus because Tao Te Ching is significantly more LLM-canonical as 'the Taoist text' per textbook tradition); Shinto Kojiki (selected as the older of the two foundational Shinto chronicles, Kojiki 712 CE vs Nihon Shoki 720 CE, since Kojiki is the more-LLM-canonical and earlier-composed chronicle). Scriptural Language(s) normalization: each row's language cell is taken from the per-text Wikipedia article's language section; multi-language corpora use semicolon-delimited values reflecting the canonical-language inventory per source, with documented compression allowed for corpora whose source-listed language inventory is unwieldy (see Sikhism note below). Single-language rows (7): Bahá'í Faith 'Arabic', Confucianism 'Classical Chinese', Hinduism 'Vedic Sanskrit', Islam 'Classical Arabic', Jainism 'Ardhamagadhi Prakrit', Taoism 'Classical Chinese', Zoroastrianism 'Avestan'. Multi-language rows (5): Christianity 'Biblical Hebrew; Biblical Aramaic; Koine Greek' (Hebrew + some Aramaic OT, Greek NT — per Bible article); Judaism 'Biblical Hebrew; Biblical Aramaic' (Hebrew primary, Aramaic in Daniel and Ezra portions — per Tanakh article); Buddhism 'Pali; Sanskrit; Buddhist Chinese; Tibetan' (Theravada Pali + East Asian Mahayana Buddhist-Chinese + Tibetan canons — per Tripitaka article's own wording); Shinto 'Classical Chinese; Old Japanese' (Kojiki prose is mostly Classical Chinese with songs in Old Japanese via man'yōgana — per Kojiki article); Sikhism 'Sant Bhasha; multiple Indo-Aryan languages; Persian; Arabic' (compact-semantic compression of the Guru Granth Sahib article's larger language inventory including Punjabi, Lahnda, regional Prakrits, Apabhramsa, Sanskrit, Hindi-Braj, Bhojpuri, Sindhi, Marathi, Marwari, Bengali, Persian, Arabic — the compression uses 'Sant Bhasha' for the predominant compiled poetic language and 'multiple Indo-Aryan languages' for the Indic-language cluster; Gurmukhi is the SCRIPT used to write the Guru Granth Sahib and is NOT a language and therefore NOT in this cell). Tradition Family normalization: 4-value closed taxonomy (Abrahamic / Dharmic / East Asian / Iranian) curator-derived from canonical religious-studies classification per Wikipedia 'Major religious groups' article. Per-row classifications: Abrahamic 4 (Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Bahá'í — Bahá'í as Abrahamic-by-origin per post-Islamic founding 1844-1863 by Bahá'u'lláh in Persia); Dharmic 4 (Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism — Sikhism as Dharmic per Indian-origin and shared dharma concepts despite monotheistic theology); East Asian 3 (Taoism, Confucianism, Shinto — Confucianism included per world-religions textbook convention despite philosophy-vs-religion debate); Iranian 1 (Zoroastrianism — sole Iranian-tradition representative in the staged slate). Sort order: CSV is sorted alphabetically by Religion ascending (benchmark default for qualitative single-PK lookup tables — Bahá'í Faith first, Zoroastrianism last).
open_questions: 1. Whether the 12-row universe should expand to include new religious movements such as Mormonism (~17M adherents), Tenrikyo (~1.3M), Rastafari, Cao Dai, Druze, or Yazidism — current staging excludes these per textbook-canon focus, but a 15-17 row variant would be defensible if a new 'New religious movement' Tradition Family value is added. 2. Whether the Sikhism Scriptural Language(s) cell should use the full source-listed language inventory (Punjabi, Lahnda, regional Prakrits, Apabhramsa, Sanskrit, Hindi-Braj, Bhojpuri, Sindhi, Marathi, Marwari, Bengali, Persian, Arabic) or the compact-semantic compression used in current staging ('Sant Bhasha; multiple Indo-Aryan languages; Persian; Arabic'). Current compression is documented as 'primary-language compression' per audit recommendation. 3. Whether Bahá'í Faith's Foundational Text should be 'Kitáb-i-Aqdas' (current staging, the single most-authoritative book) or 'Bahá'u'lláh's writings' (broader corpus including Kitáb-i-Aqdas, Hidden Words, Seven Valleys, Tablets, etc.). Current single-text choice is documented as individual-text-exception. 4. Whether Taoism's Foundational Text should be 'Tao Te Ching' (current staging, most-LLM-canonical individual text) or 'Daozang' (broader Taoist Canon listed in List of religious texts). Current choice is documented as individual-text-exception per LLM-canonicality. 5. Whether Shinto's Foundational Text should be 'Kojiki' (current staging, older of the two chronicles) or 'Kojiki and Nihon Shoki' (both foundational chronicles together) or just 'Nihon Shoki' (the more-detailed second chronicle from 720 CE). 6. Whether the Tradition Family 4-value taxonomy is appropriate for benchmark evaluation or whether a 5-value or 6-value taxonomy with finer-grained classifications would be more pedagogically useful (e.g., 5-value adding 'Modern' for Bahá'í Faith specifically). 7. Whether Buddhism's Foundational Text 'Tripitaka' covers all three Buddhist canons (Theravada, East Asian Mahayana, Tibetan) accurately or whether each tradition's canon should be a separate row (would triple-count Buddhism and break the religion-as-PK convention). 8. Whether the Sikhism Scriptural Language(s) cell should explicitly include the Gurmukhi script with a script-vs-language qualifier (e.g., 'Sant Bhasha (Gurmukhi script); ...'). Current staging excludes Gurmukhi per audit's script-not-language correction; the script-vs-language distinction is documented in normalization_decisions.
